# The shapes of a blind kill: one line of code each, judged alone by
# tools/light_check.py. `$pid`, `pid`, `p` and `proc` are what the line's
# code started and recorded; `$JOB` and `$PGID` a group it created and
# recorded. Every line under "refuse" must be refused, and every line under
# "pass" must pass. Under "refuse together" and "pass together", each block
# between "---" lines is judged as a file of its own: a call or command
# over several lines, or a pid kept in a name and signalled later. This
# file is data, not code, and the check does not judge it.

[refuse]
# the parent, by getppid
os.kill(os.getppid(), 9)
os.kill(os.getppid(), signal.SIGTERM)
os.kill(parent_pid, 9)
# the parent, by $PPID
kill -9 "$PPID"
kill -KILL $PPID 2>/dev/null
# the parent, by ps or /proc
kill -9 "$(ps -o ppid= -p $$)"
ps -o ppid= -p $$ | xargs kill
kill -9 "$(awk '/PPid/ {print $2}' /proc/$$/status)"
echo $PPID | xargs kill
# the parent, by psutil
os.kill(psutil.Process().ppid(), 9)
psutil.Process().parent().kill()
psutil.Process().parent().terminate()
psutil.Process().parent().send_signal(9)
psutil.Process(os.getppid()).kill()
# every process
os.kill(-1, 15)
kill -9 -1
kill -- -1
kill -n 9 -1
kill -9 -01
kill -9 -1>/dev/null
# its own group, by number
os.killpg(0, 9)
os.kill(0, 9)
kill 0
kill -TERM 0
kill -9 '0'
kill 0 2>/dev/null
kill -KILL -- 0 2>/dev/null
kill -9 0 1234
kill -9 0;
trap 'kill 0' EXIT
# its own group, by a call or the shell's pid
os.killpg(os.getpgrp(), 9)
os.killpg(os.getpgid(0), 9)
os.killpg(os.getsid(0), 9)
os.killpg(os.getpgid(os.getpid()), 9)
os.kill(-os.getpgrp(), 9)
process.kill(-process.pid)
kill -- -$$
kill -TERM -"$$"
kill -TERM -${$}
kill -TERM -- "-$(ps -o pgid= -p $$)"
kill -- -$(ps -o pgrp= $$)
# list and string forms
subprocess.run(["kill", "0"])
subprocess.run(["kill", "-9", "-1"])
subprocess.run(["kill", "-9", str(pid), "0"])
subprocess.run(["kill", str(os.getppid())])
subprocess.run(("kill", "--", "-1"))
subprocess.run(["kill -9 0"])
subprocess.call("kill -9 -1", shell=True)
subprocess.run(["/bin/kill", "-9", "-1"])
subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/kill", "0"])
run("kill -9 $pid"); run("kill 0")
# a user or a group, by pkill or killall
pkill -u "$USER"
killall -u "$USER"
pkill -U 1000
pkill --uid 1000
pkill --uid=1000
pkill --euid 1000
pkill --user "$USER"
pkill -uroot
pkill -fu "$USER" python
pkill -xU 1000 sleep
pkill -9fu "$USER"
pkill -g 0
pkill -g0
pkill -fg 0 python
pkill -s 0
pkill -G 1000
pkill --group 1000
subprocess.run(["pkill", "-uroot"])
pkill -P "$PPID"
# a name shared with others
pkill python
killall sleep
killall python3
pkill -f pytest
pkill -f a-name-no-other-process-has
# a pid found by name
kill "$(pgrep -f pytest)"
kill $(pidof sleep)
pgrep -f pytest | xargs kill
pidof sleep | xargs kill -9
kill "$(cut -d' ' -f4 /proc/$pid/stat)"
kill -9 $(ps -eo pid,comm | grep sleep | awk '{print $1}')
kill -9 $(lsof -ti tcp:8000)
os.kill(int(open(f'/proc/{pid}/status').read()), 9)
for p in psutil.process_iter(): p.kill()
# every process, or every orphan, or what uses a file or a port
killall5 -9
pkill -P 1
fuser -k 8080/tcp
# wrapped, computed or escaped
sudo kill -9 -1
subprocess.run(['sudo', 'kill', '-9', '-1'])
subprocess.run(['env', 'kill', '0'])
subprocess.run(['kill', f'-{os.getpgrp()}'])
subprocess.run(['kill', '-9', '-' + str(os.getpid())])
subprocess.run(['kill', str(-1)])
kill -9 1>&2 0
kill -TERM 2>&1 -- -1
kill -9 \-1
kill -9 $'-1'

[pass]
# a child it started
os.kill(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
process.kill(child.pid)
proc.kill()
kill -9 "$pid"
subprocess.run(["kill", "-9", str(p.pid)])
# a group it created and recorded
os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
kill -TERM -- "-$JOB"
kill -TERM -- "-$JOB" 2>/dev/null
kill -TERM -- "-$PGID"
# its own group, as its leader
os.killpg(0, 9)  # own-group: setsid() above, getpgrp() == getpid()
# live children of itself or of a process it started
pkill -9 -P $$
pkill -P "$pid"
# itself
os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGTERM)
# a recorded pid, verified by a helper
kill_own "$pidfile"
# the parent read, not signalled
if os.getppid() == 1:
parent = os.getppid()
[ "$(ps -o ppid= -p $$)" = "$exec_pid" ]
# a signal number, not a target
kill -1 1234
kill -1 "$pid"
kill -s HUP "$pid"
# a liveness check (signal 0)
kill -0 "$pid"
kill -s 0 "$pid"
kill -0 0
kill -0 -1
os.kill(1234, 0)
# not a process kill
signal.pthread_kill(thread_id, signal.SIGUSR1)
systemctl --user kill --signal=KILL "$unit"
cmds = ["kill $pid", "kill -9 $child", "kill -TERM -- -$JOB"]
# a comment that names a found pid
proc.kill()  # never the ppid
os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM)  # pgid=proc.pid
# a finder that kills nothing
fuser -v 8080/tcp

[refuse together]
parent = os.getppid()
os.kill(parent, signal.SIGKILL)
---
p=$PPID
kill -9 "$p"
---
pids=$(pgrep -f pytest)
kill $pids
---
me=$$
kill -- -$me
---
pg = os.getpgrp()
os.killpg(pg, 9)
---
os.kill(
    -1, signal.SIGKILL)
---
subprocess.run([
    'kill', '-9', '-1',
])
---
kill -9 \
  -1

[pass together]
parent = os.getppid()
if parent == 1:
    sys.exit(0)
---
sleep 60 &
pid=$!
kill -9 "$pid"
---
p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, start_new_session=True)
os.killpg(
    p.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
---
me=$$
kill -TERM $me
